item.title: Infinite Players: Self-Improving AI Agents In Video Games That Learn, Adapt, Remember, and Evolve Beyond Human Expertise - AERÍN Continuation Algebra, Revisable Evidence, and Semantic-Trajectory Preservation
item.description: Infinite Players develops AERÍN Continuation Algebra, a mathematical and executable research framework connecting game-agent improvement, behavioral preservation, temporal inference, revisable memory, and statistical validation. item.description: NPCs play a vital role in modern video games, making game engaging, story progress possible, and the development of a convincing virtual world. item.title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
item.description: An agent based on a large language model (LLM) may store an untrusted document and use it weeks later to select a payment destination. Preventing this action requires evidence of authorization that remains valid when stored text changes. We study a policy that requires either endorsements (explicit approvals) from two separately administered sources or explicit user authorization. item.description: Abstract Generative models often produce perceptually plausible outputs that violate hard domain rules. item.description: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. item.title: MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair
item.description: Agent memory architectures define how LLM agents store and reuse experience across tasks, but they are typically fixed after deployment, limiting their adaptability across task types. Recent self-evolving approaches instead adapt these memory architectures using execution feedback, typically represented as evaluation scores or compressed summaries. item.title: Digital Lifeforms and the Architecture of Persistent Digital Civilization
item.description: Artificial intelligence is increasingly persistent, distributed, embodied and autonomous, yet its dominant unit remains the model, agent, session or device. These units do not provide a sufficient account of identity when models are replaced, branches diverge, networks fail, bodies change, authority is revoked, or a system is reconstructed after catastrophic loss. item.title: Language modeling on tabular data: a survey of foundations, techniques and evolution
item.description: Tabular data, a prevalent data type across various domains, presents unique challenges due to its heterogeneous nature and complex structural relationships. Achieving high predictive performance and robustness in tabular data analysis holds significant promise for numerous applications. item.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. item.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
item.description: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition.
